body.heading: Small contact, real effect
paragraphs: Wellbeing advice often sounds like a shopping list of solo habits, but people are one of the basics too. A short conversation with someone you like — properly listening, not half-scrolling — does something a quiet evening alone sometimes cannot.

It does not require a big social life. One friend, one grandparent, one neighbour you chat with at the gate. Depth beats quantity here; a five-minute real exchange outranks an hour of parallel scrolling in the same room.

body.heading: Schedule it like it matters
paragraphs: Connection often loses to urgency: it is important but never the loudest item on the list. So give it a slot — the Tuesday call, the walk with a friend, the family meal that stays in the calendar.
And on the days you feel least like seeing anyone, a small dose may help most. Send the message. You rarely have to be in the mood before contact; the mood often arrives during it.

takeaway: Put people in the calendar, not just in the gaps.
